Fifty Grams of Coal

STS-HS10-L4-10001300-HSWH-LEC-CFI-01 • HS World History 10th • Why England Industrialized First
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
England did not industrialize alone, and it did not start from nothing. The printed cotton Owen is holding up copies patterns Indian artisans had perfected for centuries, and the spinning frames were built by workers whose families carried weaving skill across the Channel. Coal and machinery finished the job, but the ideas were fused from everywhere they could be borrowed. That is what Priya, Owen, and Mei are testing: not one invention, but which cause the others could not do without.
If you could keep only ONE card on that board and cut the other five, which one would you keep, and what would England lose without it?
